name: Barbell Back Squat
instructions: Bar on upper back, feet shoulder-width, sit hips back and down until thighs at least parallel, drive up through mid-foot.
precautions: Avoid if experiencing knee pain; keep knees tracking over toes; do not round lower back.

name: Goblet Squat
instructions: Hold one dumbbell vertically at chest, squat down keeping torso upright, drive through heels to stand.
precautions: Good knee-friendly alternative to barbell squat.

name: Bodyweight Squat
instructions: Feet shoulder-width, squat down until thighs near parallel, keep chest up, stand back up.
precautions: Safe for all levels; use as warm-up or high-rep conditioning.

name: Front Squat
instructions: Bar racked on front deltoids, elbows high, squat keeping torso upright.
precautions: Requires good wrist/shoulder mobility; regress to goblet squat if uncomfortable.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
instructions: Rear foot elevated on bench, front leg does the work, lower until front thigh near parallel.
precautions: Good unilateral option for limited equipment; balance-demanding.

name: Leg Press
instructions: Feet shoulder-width on platform, lower until knees near 90 degrees, press back up.
precautions: Lower-impact alternative for knee sensitivity; avoid locking knees hard at top.

name: Step-Up
instructions: Step onto a box/bench with one leg, drive through that heel to stand fully, step back down.
precautions: Use a stable low box for beginners; watch for knee valgus.

name: Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Slight knee bend, hinge at hips pushing them back, lower bar along legs, feel hamstring stretch, return to standing.
precautions: If lower back hurts, reduce load and check hip hinge form before adding weight.

name: Conventional Deadlift
instructions: Feet hip-width, grip bar outside knees, flat back, drive through floor extending hips and knees together.
precautions: High-skill lift; beginners should master hinge pattern with lighter loads first.

name: Dumbbell RDL
instructions: Hold dumbbells in front of thighs, hinge hips back keeping slight knee bend, lower to shin level, return.
precautions: Lower-load alternative to barbell RDL for beginners or lower back sensitivity.

name: Hip Thrust
instructions: Upper back on bench, bar over hips, drive hips up squeezing glutes at top, lower with control.
precautions: Excellent posterior chain builder that's gentle on the lower back.

name: Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on back, feet flat, drive hips up squeezing glutes, lower slowly.
precautions: Good rehab-friendly posterior chain exercise; no equipment needed.

name: Trap Bar Deadlift
instructions: Stand inside trap bar, grip handles, drive through floor keeping torso more upright than conventional deadlift.
precautions: More back-friendly than conventional deadlift for many lifters.

name: Bench Press
instructions: Lie on bench, bar over chest, lower to mid-chest with elbows ~45 degrees, press back up.
precautions: If shoulder pain occurs, switch to neutral-grip dumbbell press.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
instructions: Lie on bench holding dumbbells at chest level, press up until arms extended, lower with control.
precautions: Allows more natural shoulder path than barbell version.

name: Push-Up
instructions: Hands under shoulders, body in a straight line, lower chest to floor, press back up.
precautions: Use incline push-ups (hands on bench) to regress for beginners.

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
instructions: Bench set to 30-45 degrees, press dumbbells up from chest level, lower with control.
precautions: Targets upper chest; keep wrist pain-free grip angle.

name: Cable Chest Fly
instructions: Stand between cable towers, arms slightly bent, bring handles together in front of chest.
precautions: Isolation movement; use light-moderate load to protect shoulder joint.

name: Floor Press
instructions: Lie on floor, press dumbbells up from chest, upper arms stop at floor limiting range.
precautions: Reduced range of motion is easier on the shoulder joint than a full bench press.

name: Barbell Row
instructions: Hinge forward with flat back, pull bar to lower ribs, squeeze shoulder blades, lower with control.
precautions: Keep neutral spine; reduce load if lower back fatigues before back muscles.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
instructions: One knee/hand on bench for support, row dumbbell to hip, squeeze shoulder blade at top.
precautions: Great equipment-light option for a horizontal pulling pattern.

name: Seated Cable Row
instructions: Sit with knees slightly bent, pull handle to torso keeping back straight, squeeze shoulder blades.
precautions: Lower-skill alternative to barbell row for beginners.

name: Chest-Supported Row
instructions: Chest braced against pad, row weight toward torso, squeeze shoulder blades.
precautions: Removes lower back strain, good for those with back sensitivity.

name: Pull-Up
instructions: Hang from bar, pull chin over bar, lower with control.
precautions: Use resistance band assistance or lat pulldown to regress.

name: Lat Pulldown
instructions: Grip bar wider than shoulders, pull down to upper chest, control the return.
precautions: Good stepping stone toward unassisted pull-ups.

name: Resistance Band Pull-Apart
instructions: Hold band at shoulder height, pull apart squeezing shoulder blades together.
precautions: Excellent for posture and shoulder health; minimal equipment needed.

name: Overhead Press
instructions: Bar at shoulders, press overhead until arms locked out, lower with control.
precautions: If shoulder pain occurs, reduce range of motion or switch to landmine press.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
instructions: Dumbbells at shoulder height, press overhead, lower with control.
precautions: Allows a more natural shoulder path than a barbell press.

name: Landmine Press
instructions: Barbell end in landmine attachment, press diagonally up and forward from shoulder.
precautions: Shoulder-friendly pressing option for those with overhead pain.

name: Lateral Raise
instructions: Arms slightly bent, raise dumbbells out to sides to shoulder height, lower with control.
precautions: Use light weight and controlled tempo; avoid using momentum.

name: Face Pull
instructions: Pull rope/band toward face at eye level, elbows high, squeeze shoulder blades.
precautions: Great for shoulder health and posture; recommended as prehab/accessory work.

name: Bicep Curl
instructions: Elbows at sides, curl weight up toward shoulder, lower with control.
precautions: Avoid swinging body; keep elbows fixed.

name: Hammer Curl
instructions: Neutral grip, curl weight up keeping wrist neutral, lower with control.
precautions: Easier on the wrist than a standard curl for some lifters.

name: Tricep Pushdown
instructions: Elbows at sides, extend forearms down until arms straight, control the return.
precautions: Keep elbows pinned to torso throughout the movement.

name: Overhead Tricep Extension
instructions: Hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands, lower behind head, extend back up.
precautions: Avoid if shoulder mobility is limited; use lighter load.

name: Plank
instructions: Forearms and toes on floor, body in a straight line, brace core, hold position.
precautions: Stop if lower back sags; regress to knee plank.

name: Dead Bug
instructions: Lie on back, arms and legs raised, slowly extend opposite arm/leg while keeping back flat.
precautions: Excellent low-back-friendly core exercise, often used in rehab.

name: Bird-Dog
instructions: On hands and knees, extend opposite arm and leg, keep hips level, return and switch.
precautions: Recommended for those with lower back sensitivity.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
instructions: Hang from bar, raise legs to hip height or higher with control, lower slowly.
precautions: Regress to lying leg raise or knee raises if grip/core strength is limiting.

name: Cable Woodchopper
instructions: Pull cable diagonally across body from high to low (or low to high), rotate through torso.
precautions: Control the rotation; avoid using excessive load that causes jerky movement.

name: Farmer's Carry
instructions: Hold heavy weights at sides, walk a set distance keeping torso upright and shoulders back.
precautions: Great full-body/grip conditioning exercise with low injury risk.

name: Treadmill Walk/Jog
instructions: Maintain a pace that elevates heart rate to a moderate level for 20-40 minutes.
precautions: Low-impact cardio option, good for warm-up or active recovery days.

name: Jump Rope
instructions: Rotate rope and jump continuously, landing softly on the balls of the feet.
precautions: Higher impact; avoid on days with existing knee/ankle pain.

name: Stationary Bike
instructions: Pedal at a steady or interval pace for 15-30 minutes.
precautions: Very low joint impact; good option for those with knee sensitivity.

name: Rowing Machine
instructions: Drive with legs, lean back slightly, pull handle to torso, reverse the sequence to return.
precautions: Good full-body low-impact cardio; watch for lower back rounding.

name: Kettlebell Swing
instructions: Hinge at hips and snap hips forward to swing kettlebell to chest height, let it swing back between legs.
precautions: Master the hip hinge with light load first; not a squat movement.

name: Calf Raise
instructions: Rise onto toes as high as possible, pause, lower heels below platform level with control.
precautions: Simple, low-risk isolation movement for calves.

name: Walking Lunge
instructions: Step forward into a lunge, lower back knee toward floor, drive up and step through to the next lunge.
precautions: Watch front knee tracking; regress to stationary reverse lunge if balance is an issue.

name: Reverse Lunge
instructions: Step backward into a lunge, lower back knee toward floor, drive through front heel to return to standing.
precautions: Easier on the knees than a forward lunge for most beginners.

name: Cable Lateral Raise
instructions: Cable at low pulley, raise arm out to the side to shoulder height, lower with control.
precautions: Provides constant tension compared to dumbbell version.

name: Ab Rollout
instructions: Kneeling, roll wheel forward keeping core braced and back flat, roll back to start.
precautions: High core-strength demand; regress to plank progressions if lower back arches.

name: Superman
instructions: Lie face down, simultaneously lift arms, chest, and legs off the floor, hold briefly, lower.
precautions: Gentle posterior chain/lower back activation exercise, good for beginners.
